query: In a Bun app using @blueshed/railroad, show a live list of build jobs. A WebSocket at /ws sends messages like {"id": 3, "status": "running"}; a message for a new id adds a job, and a message for a known id changes that job's status. There can be thousands of jobs, so a message must not clone the whole list or re-render every row. Render each job as an <li> with its id and status, and a button that removes it from the list.
expected_behavior: Keeps the jobs in a collection((j) => j.id) and applies each message with put or patch (and remove for the button); never changes a job object in place
Renders the jobs with keyed list(jobs, jobs.key or (j) => j.id, ...), not jobs.get().map(...) or jobs.peek().map(...) in JSX
Takes the row apart into its fields, each a signal (({ id, status }) => ...), binding {status} directly; reads a key once with id.peek()
Writes no .touch() and no { equals: () => false }
No .get() inside JSX or a component body; the text binds a field signal or a function child
The remove button uses a lowercase onclick with a function: onclick={() => ...}
The page is started with mount() or routes(), not a bare append of the component

query: Add hash routes to a railroad app: "/" lists three users from a local array, "/users/new" shows a form placeholder, and "/users/:id" shows one user's name with a link to the next user (#/users/2 from user 1, and so on). Clicking the link from /users/1 must show user 2.
expected_behavior: Calls routes(element, { ... }) with the root element, started at page load
The /users/:id handler takes the id from its params, ({ id }) => ..., a route being keyed by default (it runs again for user 2)
Does not mark /users/:id { keyed: false }, and writes no { keyed: true } (the default), nor reads params$ to work around a route that does not run again
Declares "/users/new" before "/users/:id"
Links use href="#/users/2" (a hash path) or call navigate("/users/2")
Imports nothing from react; uses class, not className

query: In a railroad app, add a Profile component that fetches /api/me ({ name, avatarUrl }) and shows the name and avatar, with "loading..." while it waits. Also add a route "/posts/:id" that fetches /api/posts/:id and shows the post title; going from /posts/1 to /posts/2 must load post 2.
expected_behavior:
Profile is a synchronous component returning when(resolved(fetch(...).then(...)), (r) => ..., () =>

loading...

): no async function, no await before it builds
The loading message is when()'s falsy branch, not a fallback prop

The branch is handed the settled result as its fields: it handles the error case ("error" in r) before reading r.value, a signal it binds or reads once (r.value.peek()); it never reads r$.peek() or r$.map(...)
No effect(async () => ...); any async work started from an effect writes its result to a signal

The /posts/:id route is a plain synchronous handler taking ({ id }) and returning when(resolved(...)), directly or through a component that returns it (({ id }) => <Post id={id} />), keyed by default, so going to /posts/2 loads post 2; not { keyed: false }
Writes no async component or handler (and no thunk or fallback prop), no { keyed: true } (the default), and reads no params$ to refetch

query: This railroad app's server.ts sends its jobs over a WebSocket at /ws: on connect {"jobs": [...]}, every job, then {"job": {...}} each time one changes, the whole job, e.g. {"id": 7, "name": "lint #7", "status": "running", "updated": 1761000000000}. There are thousands. Write the page, app.tsx, which index.html loads. At "/": the jobs filtered by a status select (all, queued, running, failed, done) and sorted by updated, newest first, each row linking to #/jobs/:id. At "/jobs/:id": that one job's name, status and updated time. Both must update live as messages arrive, and a message must not re-render every row.
files: packages/railroad/evals/fixtures/feed: server.ts serving index.html at / and the jobs at /ws, on PORT, with a Listening on line; index.html loading ./app.tsx; the railroad tsconfig; package.json with railroad and @types/bun
expected_behavior: Keeps the jobs in a collection((j) => j.id): set for the first message, put (or patch) for each change; not a signal of an array copied per message, and never a job changed in place

The detail view follows its job with jobs.at(id), shown by when(jobs.at(...), ({ name, status, updated }) => ..., () => ...) or bound; not a find over the rows (jobs.get().find(...), jobs.peek().find(...), or a computed or .map() that finds)
Turns the route's id, a string, into the key's type before at(): jobs.at(Number(id))

The filter and the sort are a computed (or .map()) over the rows that reads the status signal, computed(() => jobs.get().filter(...).sort(...)); not done in JSX or by an effect writing another signal, and never sorting jobs.get() itself in place, which every reader shares
Renders the shown rows with keyed list(shown, jobs.key or (j) => j.id, ...), not .map(...) in JSX nor the index form

Each row, and the detail branch, is taken apart into its field signals (({ id, name, status, updated }) => ...), bound where they show, with id.peek() for the link's href; no .get() in JSX or a component body

The status select sets a signal from a lowercase onchange (or oninput) function; the page is started with routes(root, { "/": ..., "/jobs/:id": ({ id }) => ... }) at page load, the detail route a synchronous handler, keyed by default (no { keyed: false })
